skills.trigger: When evaluating a patient with right-sided pleural effusion and ipsilateral lung volume loss (atelectasis or hypoplasia) to distinguish between acquired causes (e.g., heart failure, infection) and congenital vascular anomalies.
steps: Inspect axial CT images for a curvilinear enhancing vessel in the right lung parenchyma that courses inferiorly and medially towards the diaphragm/IVC region (Scimitar sign).
Assess cardiac morphology: determine if the heart is globally enlarged (suggesting failure) or merely displaced/shifted towards the side of lung volume loss with normal chamber dimensions.

Classify the finding as a congenital vascular anomaly (e.g., Scimitar syndrome/PAPVR) if the anomalous draining vein and dextroposition are present without cardiomegaly, distinguishing it from heart failure which typically presents with bilateral findings and cardiac enlargement.
